prompt: in a story involving an oppressive regime, can the fighting back against them only feel satisfying if there are loads of moments where the bad guys hurt or eliminate known and fleshed out characters?
judge_reasoning: The prompt asks whether a story’s resistance to an oppressive regime can only feel satisfying if there are many scenes where the “bad guys” hurt or eliminate known, fleshed-out characters. Candidate 1 says satisfaction “does not necessarily depend” on numerous harm/elimination moments and offers alternative narrative strategies. Candidate 2 shifts to “large-scale societal suffering vs. individual character losses” and never directly answers the “only if” requirement, while Candidate 3 explains ways to portray oppression “without resorting to explicit violence against central characters,” which partially supports the prompt’s implication but doesn’t directly address satisfaction of fighting back. Candidate 4 focuses on moral dilemmas generally and is largely unrelated to whether antagonist harm/death is required for satisfaction.
